text: FCLoopAddScalingParameter[topo, la, rules] multiplies masses and momenta in the propagators of the topology topo by the scaling parameter la according to the scaling rules in rules. The id of the topology remains unchanged. This is useful e.g. for asymptotic expansions of the corresponding loop integrals given as GLIs.
The scaling variable should be declared as FCVariable via the DataType mechanism.
Notice that if all terms in a propagator have the same scaling, the scaling variable in the respective propagator will be set to unity.
We declare the external 4-momentum q as our hard scale, while the mass mc is soft

topoScaled = FCLoopAddScalingParameter[FCTopology[prop1LtopoC11, {SFAD[{{I p1, 0}, {-mc^2, -1}, 1}], SFAD[{{I (p1 - q), 0}, {-mc^2, -1}, 1}]}, {p1}, {q}, {SPD[q, q] ->mb^2}, {}], la, {q -> la^0 q, mc -> la^1 mc}]

\[\text{Scalings of momenta and masses in the propagators of }\;\text{prop1LtopoC11}\;\text{ : }\left\{\text{mb}\to \;\text{la}^0 \;\text{mb},\text{mc}\to \;\text{la} \;\text{mc},\text{p1}\to \;\text{la}^0 \;\text{p1},q\to \;\text{la}^0 q\right\}\]
Having set up the scaling we can now use FCLoopGLIExpand to expand the loop integrals belonging to this topology up to the desired order in la. Here we choose \mathcal{O}(\lambda^4)
